sections.content:
Population change in Milton Keynes in 2032

The population in Milton Keynes is projected to increase from 292,517 people in 2022 to 315,470 people in 2032.

The biggest factor in this population change is net international migration, which will increase the population by 18,045 people.

This is different to the majority of areas in England, where net internal migration is projected to be the biggest factor in population change.

sections.title: Contributors to population change in Milton Keynes
sections.subtitle: How the population is projected to change, by cause
sections.source: Subnational population projections for England from Office for National Statistics – Migration category variant
sections.note: The components of change do not always sum exactly to the total population change in an area. This is primarily due to the effect of constraining the final projections to the National Population Projections for England.

sections.content:
Population change is projected by looking at births and deaths (natural change) and people moving in and out of areas. In Milton Keynes, our projections show that between 2022 and 2032:

  • More births than deaths mean that the population is projected to increase by 8,740, with 30,774 births and 22,034 deaths in Milton Keynes between 2022 and 2032. This means natural change would increase the population in Milton Keynes by 3.0%, compared with an increase of 0.2% in England.
  • Net internal migration (people moving to and from other local authorities in England) is projected to reduce the population by 2,124, with 147,683 people moving to the area and 149,807 people moving from the area between 2022 and 2032. This would decrease the population in Milton Keynes by 0.7%.
  • Net cross-border migration (between UK nations) is projected to reduce the population by 2,009, with 3,868 people moving to the area and 5,877 people moving from the area between 2022 and 2032. This would decrease the population in Milton Keynes by 0.7%.
  • Net international migration is projected to increase the population by 18,045, with 39,748 people moving to the area and 21,703 people moving from the area between 2022 and 2032. This would increase the population in Milton Keynes by 6.2%, compared with an increase of 6.5% in England.

sections.content:
Age profile in Milton Keynes in 2032

The median age in Milton Keynes is projected to rise from 37 years in 2022 to 40 years in 2032.

In England, the median age is projected to be 41 years in 2032.

In 2032, 16% of the population in Milton Keynes are projected to be aged 65 years or over, up from 13% in 2022.

sections.title: The 0 to 9 age group are set to see the largest change in Milton Keynes between 2022 and 2032
sections.subtitle: Percentages of population by 10 year age bands, 2022 and 2032
sections.source: Subnational population projections for England from Office for National Statistics – Migration category variant

sections.content:
Between 2022 and 2032, the share of the working age population (people aged 16 years to State Pension age) in Milton Keynes is projected to stay the same, at around 66%.

The old age dependency ratio (the number of people of State Pension age for every 1,000 people of working age) is projected to rise from 202 to 219 over the same time period.

This is below average for England in 2032 (287 per 1,000). Nationally, a high old age dependency ratio means more older people are financially reliant on the working age population to pay for pensions.

How will the number of young people change in Milton Keynes?

In 2032, 22% of people are projected to be aged 18 years and under, down from 25% in 2022.

This is above average for England in 2032 (20%).

Looking at the youngest age groups in Milton Keynes between 2022 and 2032, we can see the share of:

  • Infants (aged 0 to 4 years) will fall from 6% to 5%
  • Primary school age children (aged 5 to 11 years) will fall from 10% to 8%
  • Secondary school age children and sixth-form age (aged 12 to 18 years) will stay around the same, at 8%
